method: Python Counter + difflib.SequenceMatcher (ratio>=0.82 for hi-freq pairs, >=0.85 for singleton-to-hi-freq); plus substring concept-family scan over 50 keywords; plus manual concern_text verification of every cross-concept merge.

covariate-shift (formal stats term), domain-shift (ML term), distribution-shift (umbrella) all describe feature-distribution mismatch between train and target cohorts. Specific sub-types (geographic_/temporal_/scanner_/ethnic_*_shift) are NOT merged — they carry useful sub-categorization.

imbalanced_classes/imbalanced_data are direct singleton synonyms; class_imbalance_unhandled adds a remediation-status modifier already captured by resolved/severity fields. Sub-type tags (case_control_imbalance, demographic_imbalance, temporal_imbalance, etc.) are kept distinct.

singleton "code_reproducibility" overlaps with the canonical "reproducibility" plus existing "no_code_availability"(7). llm_reproducibility, kg_reproducibility, clustering_reproducibility, architecture_reproducibility are domain-specific qualifiers and are NOT merged.

low_value_tags_to_consider_dropping.rationale: bare "overclaimed" carries no object; every concern using it also tags a specific overclaim (overclaimed_novelty, overclaimed_clinical_utility, etc.). Consider dropping or always pairing with a specific object tag.

tags_deliberately_NOT_merged.rationale: related but distinct: temporal_leakage = train/test temporal ordering violation; future_information_leakage = a future-derived feature used as input. Different MLGG gates.

no tag named "distribution_drift" exists in this KB; the variant present is "distribution_shift" (which IS merged with covariate_shift+domain_shift). "drift" tags in KB (calibration_drift_impact, definition_drift, temporal_drift, treatment_protocol_drift) refer to time-evolving processes, not cross-cohort shift.

notes.tag_cardinality_observation: KB has 2009 unique tags over 2419 instances — a 1.21 instance/tag ratio, meaning the vast majority (1801, 89.6%) appear exactly once. This is structurally worse than a synonym problem: the tag vocabulary itself is unbounded. Even after the 27 proposed merges, ~1990 unique tags remain, of which ~1797 are still singletons. Recommendation to KB maintainers: separately consider (a) introducing a controlled tag vocabulary, or (b) deprioritizing tag-overlap re-ranking in favor of category+gate+severity overlap for RAG until tag normalization is more thorough.
